SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — authored for this project's tests

# Committed warming in the Aurelian Basin may exceed assessed ranges (invented)

A fictional stand-in for a paper whose conclusions deliberately sit *above*
the assessed range — the manifest flags this document
`consensus_position: beyond-assessed-range`, and the system-prompt rule
(DESIGN.md §3.3 rule 8) requires answers drawing on it to say so. Authors
and findings are invented.

## Argument

Pellier and Vance argue that the MCA-3 assessed range for committed basin
warming (0.4–1.6 °C by 2050) understates slow feedbacks from terrace soil
carbon. Their revised estimate places committed warming at 2.1–2.8 °C —
above the assessed range — with the difference dominated by a soil-carbon
feedback the assessment treats as *low confidence*.

## Relationship to the assessed position

The authors themselves note their estimate exceeds the MCA-3 range and
attribute the gap to differing feedback treatment, not to observational
disagreement. Any answer citing this document should attribute these
figures to Pellier and Vance, and state the assessed range alongside where
it has been retrieved.

## Invented supporting estimates

Equilibrium basin sensitivity is estimated at 4.8 °C per doubling in this
paper, against the assessed 2.9–3.4 °C range.
